items.title: 68113_Barney Bigard oral history interview
items.q: So I walked over to Hodges and said, "Rab" -- we called him Rabbit -- I said, "Rab, why did you do that for? You ought to be ashamed of yourself."

ctx.x: at me, and Arthur Whetsol, he's so proper, you know, and he's looking at both of us. So when I had to wait for my turn for my solo I walked to Duke, I said, "Duke, you ought to be ashamed." He said, "Ashamed of what?" I said, "You did that." He said, "I didn't do anything." So I said, "Well, there's nobody else but Hodges."

So I walked over to Hodges and said, "Rab" -- we called him Rabbit -- I said, "Rab, why did you do that for? You ought to be ashamed of yourself." "Do what?" I said, "You know what you did." And he got angry with me.

Then the scent got stronger. It got to the first row of the people and the people began to -- everybody stirring, you know. And so Tricky, he got it too, and he started blaming me and I'm blaming him and Whetsol is blaming both of us.
